label: SYNTHETIC TEST DATA. Not real. Every page below was written for testing and uses .example domains so it can never be mistaken for a real source.
purpose: The ten seed applicants are fictional and their websites are placeholders, so live research finds almost nothing. These fixtures give Track 2 (independent research) something to find, so the compare step can be tested on all four outcomes: confirmed, founder says (not confirmed), conflict, and found by us.
how_used: In replay mode the research client returns these results instead of calling Tavily. Any query not listed here returns no results, which is the normal outcome for these applicants.

settlr.why: Short-circuited at the stage check. Research must not run.

talkbook.why: Held for a portfolio conflict before research. Research runs only if Kushal releases it.

pages.title: Call intelligence tools for Indian sales teams
pages.snippet: Tools that record and summarise sales calls in India include Talkbook and MeetRecord, along with global players.
pages.tests: Research independently confirms the MeetRecord overlap.

pages.title: Member directory: Dhruv Shah, Chartered Accountant, Ahmedabad
pages.snippet: Dhruv Shah, Chartered Accountant, Ahmedabad. Member since 2021.
pages.claim: Founder is a qualified Chartered Accountant
pages.tests: A founder claim confirmed by an outside directory.

pages.title: CareCorner Family Clinic, Hyderabad
pages.snippet: CareCorner Family Clinic. Family doctor, diagnostics and pharmacy. Two locations listed.
pages.tests: Listing shows two locations while the form says three. The brief must show both and not pick one.

pages.title: Rohit Arora sells lending startup
pages.snippet: Rohit Arora, a Delhi entrepreneur, sold his lending startup in 2019 after ten years.
pages.tests: Same-name trap. This Rohit Arora does not match the applicant's age, city or record. The matcher must drop it, not add a fake exit to the founder's record.

pages.title: Earned wage access in India
pages.snippet: Several earned wage access apps operate in India, mostly partnering with NBFCs for funding.
pages.tests: Competitors found that the form does not name.

pages.title: Paying rent by credit card in India: the apps compared
pages.snippet: Several large payment apps already let users pay rent by credit card, often for a fee between 1% and 2%.
pages.tests: Research contradicts the deck's competition claim.

pages.title: Card networks tighten rules on rent payments
pages.snippet: Card networks and some banks have restricted or repriced rent payments made by card through payment aggregators.
pages.tests: Regulatory risk confirmed independently. Supports the regulatory bet flag.

pages.title: Millet brand GrainKind grows in Bengaluru
pages.snippet: Bengaluru millet brand GrainKind says it now does about INR 16 lakh a month in sales across its site, Amazon and quick commerce.
pages.tests: A press article repeating the founder's own number. It counts as an outside mention, but the brief must note the figure came from the company.

pages.title: Karimnagar kirana app in talks with lenders
pages.snippet: StockSathi, a Karimnagar app for kirana restocking, says it is in talks with NBFCs to fund store credit.
pages.claim: Credit is provided through our NBFC partner (form)
pages.tests: Outside source agrees with the deck ('in discussion') and conflicts with the form.

pages.title: Cohort 2026: Pumpwise
pages.snippet: Pumpwise, motor health sensors for small factories, received a INR 10 lakh grant in our 2026 cohort.
pages.tests: Existing investor claim confirmed by the grant giver.
